findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: similar, opinion, statute, corrections_policy · Private data: search, fts, semantic_search, similar, citation, opinion, citations, parentheticals, treatment, brief_check, statute_citing, corrections_policy, deadline, sources · Public sink: statute_search, corrections_policy, deadline · Destructive: statute_search.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: similar, opinion, statute, corrections_policy · Private data: search, fts, semantic_search, similar, citation, opinion, citations, parentheticals, treatment, brief_check, statute_citing, corrections_policy, deadline, sources · Public sink: statute_search, corrections_policy, deadline · Destructive: statute_search

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "corrections_policy" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
